Tournament admin redesign · Stage 5 addendum · drawn 12 Oct 2026

Event settings, in the kit’s look

⚖ Ruled 12 Oct 2026 · every recommendation · build prompt written

The owner, 12 Oct: “agree with your recommendations” — A71–A77 as recommended. The build starts from docs/projects/archive/TOURNAMENT_ADMIN_REDESIGN_EVENT_SETTINGS_BUILD_PROMPT.md in a new chat. The asks below keep their recommended answers as the record of the ruling. Plan of record: TOURNAMENT_ADMIN_REDESIGN_PLAN.md §6e, “Stage 5 addendum: Event settings in the kit’s look”.

“looks like event settings has not gone through our format consistency work, this looks like some of the older fonts and look, can you review?” … “why do we have the ‘org address’ in the event settings? that is not tied to a specific event” … “review the navigation on these pages. when I go to manage questions, it brings me to a new page (should be a drawer over the page based on our standard), but also the ‘back’ button brings me to settings, which after going there, doesn’t have a button in settings to get back to the registrations questions”

Stage 5 ruled Event settings “the model” for how a setup screen saves (it saves as you go), and left its look alone apart from one card. This sheet captures today’s page on the event you were on, UAT Stage 3 Walk, at 1440 and 390, and redraws every card in the look that one card already has. Everything below was measured in the running product; nothing was saved while measuring.

1 of 7 cards already in the kit’s look (Fees & payments) 10 field names in spaced capitals 22 setting names in typewriter capitals 12 on/off settings as ON / OFF buttons, 24px tall at a desk 4 one-value choices as button rows The workspace address: 2 places, 2 names

Recommended, in one list

  1. Every card in the look Fees & payments already has (A71): field names in sentence case, plain bold setting names, the house’s text sizes, 16px card titles. Same cards, same order, same save-as-you-go.
  2. The kit’s controls (A72): an on/off setting is a switch row; a choice of one value is a dropdown with its sentence under it; a locked format reads as its value.
  3. Tie-breakers on the reorder standard (A73), here and in a division’s form, which uses the same list.
  4. Registration questions live in their card (A74), a question opening its own window over Event settings, as every other setup list works. The separate page goes, and with it the wrong back link.
  5. The web address moves to Settings & access (A75), with one name.
  6. The stragglers (A76): the Teams page’s add-team form and the bracket editor still wear the old capitalised labels.
  7. On a phone a card opens in place (A77), as the portal’s Team settings does; a window (a question, the web address) fills the screen with a back arrow at the top.

What the page does today

  1. F108

    Two looks on one page. Stage 5 rebuilt one card, Fees & payments, on the kit: a dropdown with its sentence under it, a switch row, a door to each division’s fee (E3). The six others still use the old public-site screen’s stylesheet: 10 field names in spaced capitals (“TOURNAMENT NAME”), 22 setting names in typewriter capitals (“LIST IN PUBLIC TOURNAMENT DIRECTORY”), notes in italics, and text at 12.8px, 11.5px and 15px where the house uses 14 and 12. Card titles are 14px in Title Case; the house’s card title is 16px in sentence case. Payment instructions, inside the rebuilt card, kept the typewriter label.

    Fixed by A71: every card drawn below.
  2. F109

    Twelve on/off settings are ON / OFF button pairs: 11px capitals, 24px tall at a desk, under the admin’s 34px (Stage 5’s walks found this and recorded it). On a phone each pair is a full-width 44px bar. The rebuilt card’s one setting is a switch, so the page has two controls for the same job. Post-event results says Enabled / Disabled where the rest say On / Off.

    Fixed by A72: switch rows.
  3. F110

    Four choices of one value are button rows: Game timing, Tie-breaker rules, Registration alert routing and Score finalization. Your August convention says a choice of one value is a dropdown; Fees’ Fee model already is one. Once the event leaves Draft, Tournament format shows its three buttons greyed, with the lock explained in italics underneath.

    Fixed by A72: dropdowns; the locked format reads as its value.
  4. F111

    The tie-breaker list has a look of its own: 13px names, an 11px “ADD”, typewriter chips, a × on every row, and a 19px drag handle with no way to reorder on a phone. A division’s form uses the same list, so the converted division record carries it too.

    Fixed by A73: the reorder standard you ruled today.
  5. F112

    The workspace’s web address is changed from one event’s settings. It is the start of every tournament’s link, and the owner sees it on every plan, so a League or Club owner can change it here and in the organization’s Settings, where it is called “URL slug”. One thing, two places, two names. It came here in June because the tournament plans had no settings screen of their own and the address needed a home inside the tournament admin. Settings & access exists now.

    Answered by A75.
  6. F113

    Manage questions leaves for a page with no home. From Event settings it opens a separate page. Its back link says “Settings” and opens Settings & access, the rail lights Settings & access rather than Event settings, and Settings & access has no door back to the questions. Opened from the Teams page, the same page’s back link says “Registrations”, a name the rail no longer uses.

    Answered by A74.
  7. F114

    A double period in the turnover example: “… no earlier than 9:45 a.m..”.

    Fixed in the drawing (no ask).

The alternative · A74 B

Manage questions opens a window over Event settings

What you described. It works, and it is the right shape for a long list. For this one I recommend the card instead, because every other setup list in the admin already works that way: Divisions, Venues and Rules & resources show their list on the page and open each record in a window. Here a question would open a second window on top of the list’s window, two layers for a list that is usually a handful of questions.

Notes

What rides without an ask

Carried by the build

  • The double period in the turnover example (F114).
  • The two “are you sure” boxes on this page (changing the event’s link, changing the address) move to the kit’s asking window, with today’s words.
  • The help article for Event settings and its Registration questions link follow the build (the help’s link opens the card).
  • The tie-breakers keep their own names (Head-to-Head, Run Diff, Runs For, Runs Against, Coin Toss): they are the standings’ column words.

The /design review, 12 Oct: four findings, all applied

  • D1 · The order handles are drawn as built: borderless, a grip on the questions (they have no numbers) and the grip with the olive number on the tie-breakers; 44px on a phone, where only the numbered one has a border.
  • D2 · Add a question sits above the list it fills, at the right of the card’s first line, as Rules puts Add a section in its section’s head; a phone shows the + alone.
  • D3 · The address window’s field says “Address”, not the window’s own title again.
  • D4 · The six coach emails follow their switch with no drawn rule beside them (the kit has none); with the switch off they dim, as the kit’s off row does.

Not touched

  • What any setting does, its default, or who can change it.
  • The order of the cards and of the settings inside them.
  • Saving as you go and the floating “Saved”.
  • The status line and Change, which opens the event’s record (Stage 5, A49).
